_about: Chester (the Roodee) for tools/course/real/layout.py. Ring 1 = OSM's inner edge of the turf, taken as the inside rail (offset 0); its points run anticlockwise, the running direction. Ring 0 = the outer edge. The home straight is the long north-east side under the County Stand and Nun's Road (the enclosures and parade ring are in the infield beside it); the far side runs along the railway (west) and the river (south). The chute is the wedge at the south-east corner by Grosvenor Road (the 1m2f75y and 2m2f147y, 'in a chute at the top of the home straight', geegeez): its outer edge (points 39 to 38) is the chute's outer rail. The spur off the north corner is not used. Chester is nearly circular, 1,654 m round OSM's inner edge (1m73y), so most races go round more than once: each route runs the laps it needs and the post is found on its last lap (searchLast). Starts in At The Races' order, all twelve on or beside a bend (only the chute starts are on a straight).
